$comment: Schema and example for docs/sprint-logs/{SprintID}/verify-run.json — the MACHINE-AUTHORED test result, written by hooks/run-verify.py. It is the trust source for test status: sprint done's gate and the verification-integrity hook read this, NOT the model's hand-written verification-results.json. Models MUST NOT edit this file. See references/verify-execution.md.

$rules.producer: hooks/run-verify.py only. The model never authors or edits verify-run.json or the verify-run-*.log files.
$rules.ground_truth: Each run's real process exit code. It is also written into the tail of docs/sprint-logs/{SprintID}/verify-run-{name}.log as `__VERIFY_EXIT_CODE__:{name}:{code}` so status can be re-derived even if this JSON is tampered with.
$rules.machine_status_rule: A run is `pass` iff exit_code == 0 AND (no JUnit, or JUnit failed+errored == 0). The JUnit cross-check defends against runners that exit 0 despite failing cases. overall_machine_status is `pass` iff every run is `pass`.
$rules.language_agnostic: Relies only on POSIX exit codes (universal) and optional JUnit XML (emitted by virtually every framework: gotestsum, pytest --junitxml, jest-junit, playwright junit reporter, rspec, maven-surefire, …). No framework-specific output parsing.
$rules.command_source: Where the command list came from: 'declared (.claude/verify.json)' | 'fallback (make verify)' | 'fallback (make test)'. If unconfigured, run-verify.py exits 2 and writes nothing — that is a GAP (blocks done), never a pass.
$rules.freshness: run-verify.py deletes prior verify-run-*.log and verify-run.json before each run, so the artifact reflects only the latest run (re-running after a fix is not contaminated by the previous failure).
$rules.backward_compatibility: Optional / on-demand. Absent ⇒ machine verification was not run for this Sprint; sprint done treats that as a gap to surface (not a silent pass) unless the project has no verify command configured at all.
